div.p: Parse Markdown and code-shaped AI output, retain addressable structure, render D2 or Mermaid to SVG, project the same entities into Cytoscape or XYFlow, and track every state through source revisions and human layout edits.

Any Markdown, code, D2, Mermaid, SVG, table, or AI message can become an addressable artifact graph. D2 file edits from Git are the first input fixture. The same mechanism later accepts automatically captured D2 fences and structured overrides emitted in AI messages.

Resource identity and placement identity remain separate. A node can retain its entity identity while moving between Dockview, a rectangular grid, XYFlow, Cytoscape, an SVG document, or a detached window.

g.text: Geometry mechanics available from existing platforms and libraries

ul.li: content identity comes from hashes and parsed IDs

div.p: Cache every scrapeable fenced block with message ID, ordinal, language, optional fence name, source offsets, and content hash. Initial languages: d2, mermaid, svg, json, and jsoncanvas.
Parse headings, lists, tables, links, code fences, symbols, file paths, and explicit IDs. Preserve byte spans and source text so a generated graph always points back to exact material.
These examples reserve an addressable output shape. Message parsing and authority rules are handled separately.

pre.code: type ArtifactId = string type RevisionId = string type EntityId = string type ViewId = string

div.p: Artifact IDs address a logical board or document. Revision IDs address immutable source states. Entity IDs survive revisions. View IDs address mutable placements.

pre.code: type ArtifactRevision = { artifactId: ArtifactId revisionId: RevisionId parentRevisionIds: RevisionId[] source: SourceRef contentHash: string capturedAt: string }

div.p: Prefer explicit D2 dotted IDs or authored IDs. Fallback addresses combine structural kind, ancestor heading path, fence name or ordinal, source span, and a content fingerprint. Source spans locate text but do not serve as persistent identity.
Preserve dotted IDs, containers, classes, labels, shapes, links, edges, and source spans. Rendered SVG group classes currently carry base64-encoded dotted IDs.
Preserve diagram kind, authored node IDs, subgraphs, edge endpoints, labels, classes, and source spans. Normalize only after retaining the language-specific syntax tree.

Build an AST index over headings, blocks, tables, list items, links, fences, symbols, and byte spans. Convert explicit relations into graph edges. Tables can become nodes, attributes, or relations according to a declared projection.

pre.code: type Entity = { id: EntityId kind: string label?: string attrs: Record<string, unknown> sourceSpans: SourceSpan[] }

div.p: Nodes, typed edges, containment, groups, references, source provenance, and revision membership. Parallel edges receive stable IDs independent of geometry.
PlacementMode enumerates dock, grid, canvas, window, and svg.
Human movement writes placement events. It does not rewrite D2 topology unless an explicit source-edit command requests that conversion.

Append source revisions, parsed entity diffs, placement changes, selection, camera, panel composition, overrides, undo, and redo. Fold events into current state and retain revision-addressable snapshots or checkpoints.
D2 or Mermaid source plus renderer version, layout engine, theme, fonts, and options. Cache key: source hash plus every render-affecting option.
Retain the complete SVG, viewBox, element transforms, paths, bounds, and source ID mapping. SVG is both a display artifact and a geometry carrier.

Normalize nested transforms into world coordinates. Extract node rectangles, centers, ports, label boxes, edge paths, path lengths, and container bounds. Map every geometry record back to an entity ID.

ul.li: SVG document viewer retains renderer output exactly.
Cytoscape receives nodes, edges, and preset positions.
XYFlow receives custom nodes, handles, edges, and viewport state.
Dockview and rectangular grids host any of these views as panels.

div.p: For revisions R0 -> R1, compute keep, enter, exit, and update by entity ID. One diff feeds SVG, Cytoscape, XYFlow, tables, trees, and side panels. Coordinates are observations and never keys.
Interpolate translation, size, opacity, color, and transform. CSS transitions, WAAPI, Motion, or renderer-native animation cover matching numeric properties.

CSS interpolates d only when command structure and point counts are compatible. General edge morphing needs path normalization or resampling. Preserve edge identity, sample both paths by arc length, align direction, then interpolate corresponding points.

Derive entry origin from authored or inferred parent, predecessor, group centroid, or nearest retained neighbor. Exit reverses the same rule. Final positions remain those produced by D2/Mermaid or a user placement view.

Coalesce edits while the source is changing. Render after a configurable quiet window, cancel superseded work, and retain only requested intermediate revisions. Git playback can render ahead and cache. Interactive dragging updates placement without rerendering source diagrams.

getBBox, getCTM, DOMMatrix, DOMPoint, getTotalLength, and getPointAtLength provide bounds, transform flattening, and arc-length sampling. requestAnimationFrame, Web Animations API, and CSS transitions provide scheduling and interpolation.

flubber supplies shape/path interpolation. d3-interpolate-path extends paths to compatible command sequences. svg-path-properties supplies length and point sampling outside the browser. svgpath applies and normalizes path transforms.

Cytoscape preset layout consumes extracted D2 positions. Cytoscape layouts and plugins cover animated layout, fCoSE, ELK, Dagre, Cola, compound nodes, and viewport fitting. XYFlow supplies measured node dimensions, coordinate conversion, viewport operations, and custom edge paths.

RBush indexes rectangles for hit testing and visible-region queries. d3-quadtree covers point proximity. d3-delaunay supplies nearest-neighbor and Voronoi geometry. ELK or Dagre covers layered placement; constraint or packing layouts can operate on a placement view without changing the source graph.
Daily-driver shell, Dockview, terminal/file/media resources, D2/Mermaid preview, persistence experiments, canvas/window algebra, source watching, and command bus.
Reusable signal-driven Dockview plus XYFlow composition, rectangle state, grid stack, event folding, and viewport-culling receipts.
Atlas model, keyed graph transitions, tours, D2 ingestion, Cytoscape renderer, synchronized side panels, SQLite row ingestion, and Git-to-frame machinery.
Stable relational identities, graph facts, VS Code flow panel, D2 emitters, graph queries, source relations, and revision-aware analytical projections.
Plans mention sprefa/REPORT-D2ANIM-B.md, which is absent. Its findings appear in sprefa/plans/2026-08-08-d2-svg-cytoscape-report.md.
